newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - PGMs to remain volatile, gold limited.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - PGMs to remain volatile, gold limited.

text.p: SPOT NY CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Further volatility is forecast for the very tight platinum and palladium markets on Monday.
Analysts said that in the continuing absence of Russian exports, further spikes higher were inevitable, but established resistance levels for gold and silver prices were likely to hold.
PLATINUM/PALLADIUM
Lack of liquidity in the platinum and, especially, palladium markets will mean that prices are open to being shunted up and down on the back of fairly light volumes, dealers said.
The overall movement was likely to be upwards, however, at least until the Russians belatedly began their 1997 export campaign.

"The (PGM) markets are very nervous. With a $30 spread, it only takes two to three trades to push the price $60 higher, so people can take it wherever they want for a few hundred ounces," one dealer said.
Further, the charts at these levels were so sparse that technical analysis was limited.
Even so, psychological pressure could be expected at $500.00 per ounce, where nerve failed a couple of times late last week.
But upward pressure could come into platinum as leases expired and consumers of the metal were forced to buy rather than renew leases.
"If there is no forward market they cannot offer lease rates," one dealer said.
Countering that technically, with an RSI of 84, platinum was signalling it was overbought.
At 0710 GMT platinum was indicated at $470.00/$500.00, about five dollars below the Friday London close.
GOLD -
Prices began to respond to the tearaway style of platinum and palladium towards the end of last week, but a serious breakout was unlikely, analysts said.
"Gold will have to break resistance at $347.00 to make headway, and that will not be easy," one analyst said.
He added that support was now well established at $339-$340.
"It is difficult to see gold breaking out with summer coming on and the market getting quieter," a dealer said.
At 0720 gold was indicated at $344.30/$344.80, just 10 cents above London's Friday close.
SILVER -
Attempts to take silver higher have been frustrated twice in the past 10 days and there was little follow-through to Friday's $4.90 fix, the highest since April 2.
"You could still expect a 25-30 cent move in one day for silver," an analyst said.
The price was stuck in the middle of a tight range, however, with resistance likely at $4.92 and support indicated at $4.75.
Analyst said the market was attracting short-term speculation, which could account for recent fluctuations.
At 0720 silver was indicated at $4.81/$4.83, down seven cents from Friday's close.
--Brian Spoors, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8058
